blizzwatch-sky.name: Blizzard Watch: getting Skyborne to Stormwind and Orgrimmar

facts.t: Horde races: Orc, Undead, Tauren, Troll and the new Windshaper Skyborne.
Undead are the Horde's only Paladins, a pairing new in Forever.
Horde made up 51.4% of beta characters.
Horde and Alliance still can't group together.
Alliance races: Human, Dwarf, Night Elf, Gnome and the new High Order Skyborne.
Dwarves are the Alliance's only Shamans, a pairing new in Forever.
Alliance made up 48.6% of beta characters overall, but 50.9% on the PvP ruleset.
Horde and Alliance still can't group together.

races.name: Orc
races.look: Broad, green-skinned and tusked, with heavy shoulders and a brawler's forward lean.
races.lore: Free of their demonic past, orcs fight for honor and a homeland in a world that distrusts them.

racials.name: Blood Fury
racials.t: +10% Attack Power and Spell Power for 15 sec. Cooldown back to 2 min (was 3 in the beta).

racials.name: Shatter Curse
racials.t: Now dispels Curses and Banes, and cuts magic damage taken by 5% (was 15%).

racials.name: Command
racials.t: Hunter and Warlock pets deal 5% more damage. Replaces Savage.

racials.name: Hardiness
racials.t: Stuns on you last 20% shorter.

facts.t: Orc Mage is one of six race and class pairings new in Forever.

races.name: Undead
races.look: Gaunt and half-decayed, with glowing eyes and bare bone; eerie, hunched and theatrical.
races.lore: Former humans who broke free of the Lich King, now seeking survival and revenge under Sylvanas.

racials.name: Will of the Forsaken
racials.t: Removes Charm, Fear and Sleep, but no longer grants immunity afterward.

racials.name: Cannibalize
racials.t: Eat a corpse to regenerate 35% of your Health, and now Mana too.

racials.name: Underwater Breathing
racials.t: Breathe 300% longer underwater.

racials.name: Touch of the Grave
racials.t: Attacks may drain health: 30% chance for casters, 20% for melee. Cooldown now 15 sec (was 25).

facts.t: Undead Paladin is new in Forever and the Horde's only Paladin.
Undead Paladin was the most-created race and class pair in the beta, at 6.0%.

races.name: Tauren
races.look: Huge, horned and hooved, with braids and totems; gentle giants who move with calm weight.
races.lore: Plains folk of Mulgore who honor the Earth Mother and joined the Horde after the orcs aided them.

racials.name: War Stomp
racials.t: Stuns nearby enemies for 2 sec. Cooldown now 90 sec (was 2 min).

racials.name: Cultivation
racials.t: Grows a bonus herb anyone can pick, no Herbalism needed. Cooldown now 15 min.

racials.name: Plainsrunning
racials.t: Run speed builds 2% per stack while you keep moving, up to 60% (was 30%). No longer boosts mounted speed.

racials.name: Endurance
racials.t: +5% total Health. The critical damage and healing bonus was removed.

races.name: Troll
races.look: Tall and lanky, blue- or green-skinned, with tusks, wild hair and a loping crouch.
races.lore: The Darkspear tribe, driven from their jungle islands, found refuge and honor in Thrall's Horde.

racials.name: Berserking
racials.t: +10% casting and attack speed for 15 sec (was 10).

racials.name: Rapid Regeneration
racials.t: Regenerate 50% of your maximum Health over time.

racials.name: Beast Slaying
racials.t: +5% damage against Beasts.

racials.name: Regeneration
racials.t: 20% of your health regeneration continues during combat (was 10%).

facts.t: Troll Warlock is one of six race and class pairings new in Forever.

races.name: Windshaper Skyborne
races.look: Slender, airy elves with feathered hair and wind tattoos, from sky-blue to darker skin tones.
races.lore: Highborne descendants raised by Skywall's wind spirits, searching for their vanished elemental mentors.

racials.name: Walk on Air
racials.t: Glide gently downward through the air for 10 sec. Cooldown now 90 sec (was 2 min).

racials.name: Skysight
racials.t: 15% faster run speed for 15 sec. At an elemental convergence: 30% for 1 hour, even through death.

racials.name: Wind Blessed
racials.t: +2% Haste for melee, ranged and spells (was 3%).

racials.name: Elemental Insight
racials.t: +5% damage against Elementals.

facts.t: They start on Zephras Isle, a new sky-island zone for levels 1–12.
After Zephras Isle, a skycutter carries Windshapers toward Thunder Bluff; Skyborne have no capital of their own.
Skyborne Druid was the most-created Windshaper pairing in the beta, at 2.9%.

races.name: Human
races.look: Familiar, balanced proportions: the everyday hero, from farmhand to shining knight.
races.lore: A young, adaptable people rebuilding Stormwind's glory after generations of war.

racials.name: Will to Survive
racials.t: Break free of stun effects.

racials.name: Perception
racials.t: Detect stealthed enemies for 20 sec.

racials.name: Ruthless
racials.t: +1% critical strike chance (was 2%). Replaces Sword Specialization.

racials.name: The Human Spirit
racials.t: +10% Spirit (was 5%).

facts.t: Human Hunter is one of six race and class pairings new in Forever.

races.name: Dwarf
races.look: Short, stout and barrel-chested, with grand braided beards; cheerful mountain folk.
races.lore: Ironforge miners turned explorers, digging through old records of their titan-forged origins.

racials.name: Stoneform
racials.t: Immune to Bleeds, Poisons and Diseases, and less Physical damage taken, for 8 sec.

racials.name: Find Treasure
racials.t: Track treasure chests, now with a chance of extra items in most chests.

racials.name: Artisan's Precision
racials.t: +1% hit chance with spells and attacks. Replaces Earth Fury.

racials.name: Big Game Hunter
racials.t: +5% damage against Beasts.

facts.t: Dwarves are the Alliance's only Shamans, new in Forever.
Dwarf Shaman reached 4.1% of all beta characters.

races.name: Night Elf
races.look: Tall, slender and violet-skinned, with long ears and softly glowing eyes.
races.lore: Ancient forest guardians stepping out of long isolation to face the Burning Legion again.

racials.name: Elune's Light
racials.t: +10% critical strike chance for 15 sec.

racials.name: Shadowmeld
racials.t: Slip into stealth while standing still.

racials.name: Quickness
racials.t: +1% Dodge and +2% run speed, now stacking with other speed boosts.

racials.name: Wisp Spirit
racials.t: Move 75% faster while dead.

races.name: Gnome
races.look: Tiny, big-headed and bright-eyed, with wild hair; quick and curious tinkerers.
races.lore: Brilliant inventors who lost their city to invasion and now live and work beside the dwarves.

racials.name: Escape Artist
racials.t: Brief immunity to roots and snares.

racials.name: Eureka!
racials.t: An 8-sec buff: cheaper abilities and 10% more direct damage or healing.

racials.name: Expansive Mind
racials.t: +5% maximum Mana, Rage or Energy.

racials.name: Engineering Specialization
racials.t: Your engineering devices are more reliable.

facts.t: Gnome Priest is new in Forever, with its own racial Priest spells.

races.name: High Order Skyborne
races.look: The same airy, feathered elves, dressed in a scholarly, arcane-robed style.
races.lore: Heirs of Eldre'Thalas scholars, returning to Azeroth to reclaim lost arcane knowledge.

racials.name: Walk on Air
racials.t: Glide gently downward through the air for 10 sec. Cooldown now 90 sec (was 2 min).

racials.name: Read Leyline
racials.t: +50% Health and Mana regeneration for 15 sec. At a Ley Line: +100% for 1 hour. Not during Innervate.

racials.name: Wind Blessed
racials.t: +2% Haste for melee, ranged and spells (was 3%).

racials.name: Elemental Insight
racials.t: +5% damage against Elementals.

facts.t: They start on Zephras Isle, a new sky-island zone for levels 1–12.
High Order Skyborne are the only Skyborne who can be Mages.
After Zephras Isle, a skycutter carries the High Order to Dalaran, with a portal on to Stormwind.
Victory Rush arrives at 20: an instant strike after a kill that heals 10% of your max health.
Blizzard: Warriors handle many melee foes at once but have few ways to recover from heavy damage.
Every race on both factions can be a Warrior, Skyborne included.

specs.name: Arms
specs.fantasy: A disciplined weapon master who waits for the opening, then lands one crushing blow.

leveling.t: Rage was rebalanced for questing armor on Oct 8, so most Warriors now gain more Rage while leveling.
Several leveling lists rank Warrior slowest solo: gear-reliant, little self-healing, but strong in groups.

group.t: Battle Shout now buffs your whole raid, not just your party.
Beta tier lists place Arms mid-pack for PvE damage, usually behind Fury.

pvp.t: Spearing Strike dismounts riders and deals double damage to mounted foes, Dragons and Giants.
At level 30, casters could kite Warriors until geared; a level-60 spike is expected but untested.

difficulty.t: Rage pooling, stance swaps and Overpower timing; Rage can feel slow early on.

gear.t: Damage leans on weapon quality, so every weapon upgrade feels big while leveling.

changes.t: Weaponmaster: one talent replaces every weapon specialization, tuned to the weapon you hold.
Bloodthrill: hits on targets with your Rend can light up Overpower (20% chance).
Shield Wall, Recklessness and Retaliation no longer share a cooldown.

specs.name: Fury
specs.fantasy: A roaring storm of twin blades, fed by rage and never slowing down.

leveling.t: An Oct 2 rework gave Fury more early leveling tools, like Lingering Rage to slow Rage decay.
Fury kills quickly but takes a lot of damage, so expect more breaks to recover.

group.t: Beta tier lists often rate Fury the strongest Warrior damage spec.
In Classic Era, Warriors filled many raid slots, with Fury as the main melee damage.

pvp.t: Rated strong in PvP once geared, especially in battlegrounds with a healer behind you.

difficulty.t: A priority rotation with Rage and off-hand hits to manage.

gear.t: Dual-wield damage depends on two good weapons, plus hit and crit.

changes.t: Whirlwind always hits with both weapons, and Raging Blows makes Cleave and Whirlwind cheaper.
Bloodthirst no longer heals; it grants 10% movement speed instead.
New Gore Drinker talent adds small heals after Enrage effects; Flurry now needs Death Wish.

specs.name: Protection
specs.fantasy: An unbreakable shield wall that plants its feet and dares the enemy closer.

leveling.t: Thunder Clap now works in Defensive Stance, and Vanguard lets you Charge from it.
Some guides now suggest a shield build for solo play; others still prefer Arms.

group.t: Blizzard: any party or raid is happy to add a Warrior, as tank or damage dealer.
Tank lists rate it solid, usually just behind Prot Paladin at level 30.

pvp.t: Blizzard opened a shield-free path into mid-Protection as a PvP secondary spec.
As a full spec, Protection is rated low for PvP.

difficulty.t: Threat, Rage and cooldown timing; Rage is now more forgiving for tanks.

gear.t: Defense and shield gear matter for raids, but armor no longer starves your Rage.

changes.t: Rage from damage taken ignores Armor and absorbs, even Power Word: Shield.
Vanguard lets you Charge while in Defensive Stance.
Blocks, dodges and parries can each grant 5 Rage through talents.

facts.t: Judgement no longer consumes your Seal, so you recast less.
Paladins still lack an interrupt and a real slow, but shine against Undead and Demons.
Undead Paladins are new on the Horde; Humans and Dwarves remain the Alliance Paladins.

specs.name: Holy
specs.fantasy: A steady beacon of Light, mending allies with bright, decisive heals.

leveling.t: Bonus healing now also grants a third as much bonus damage, which helps healers quest.
Guides advise against leveling as a pure healer, though a spell-power Shockadin can hit surprisingly hard.

group.t: Blizzard calls Paladins the strongest single-target healers; group healing takes more planning.
Tier lists split: one rates Holy highly, another says it lags; some players worry about mana.

pvp.t: Voice of Truth grants brief immunity to Silence and interrupts.
Rated strong for PvP at level 30: durable, if light on burst.

difficulty.t: Infusion of Light rewards rotating Holy Shock, Flash of Light and Holy Light while watching mana.

gear.t: Wants healing power and Intellect; Reverence adds Spirit regen while casting.

changes.t: Holy Shock is now the 21-point talent, with a much shorter cooldown than before.
Light's Vigil (31-point) resets Holy Shock and can spread its healing to the ally's party.
Infusion of Light: Holy Shock or Flash of Light crits speed up your next Holy Light.

specs.name: Protection
specs.fantasy: A holy bulwark wrapped in Light, shielding friends and judging the wicked.

leveling.t: Blocks and Seal of Fury absorbs return mana; Shield Specialization was trimmed to 4% on Oct 15.
Protection can pull several enemies and burn them down with Consecration; mana is the main limit.

group.t: Judging with Seal of Fury taunts, a tool Classic Paladins never had.
Beta tier lists widely name Prot Paladin the top tank at level 30.

pvp.t: Rated mid for PvP: with no interrupt or slow, it plays as a durable, supportive pick.

difficulty.t: Taunting is tied to Seal and Judgement timing; Swift Judgement gives one reset if it misses.

gear.t: Wants a mix of spell power and defense, a gearing niche of its own.

changes.t: Seal of Fury adds Holy damage to each swing plus small absorbs, and its Judgement taunts.
Templar's Bulwark (21-point): a big, short absorb shield based on your max health, on a long cooldown.
Iron Creed turns well-timed Holy Strikes into less damage taken.

specs.name: Retribution
specs.fantasy: A crusader swinging a mighty two-hander, every strike sealed with holy judgement.

leveling.t: Holy Strike damage per rank was raised so each new rank feels like an upgrade.
Sources split: some call it a steady, slow-but-safe leveler; others rate it easy and strong.

group.t: Sacred Arbiter empowers Holy Strike and refreshes your Judgements on the target.
Rankings disagree: top tier on one beta list, behind for now on another.

pvp.t: Repentance is now a 21-point talent (was 31), so it's easier to reach.

difficulty.t: A simple core loop; Seal twisting is optional through a talent.

gear.t: Wants a strong two-hander, ideally with spell power; Intellect also feeds spell damage.

changes.t: Twist of Light (31-point) lets you twist Seals without a swing-timer addon.
Vengeance was redesigned: up to 3 stacks, triggered by critical strikes.
Champion of the Light turns 10/20/30% of your Intellect into spell damage (lowered Oct 15).

facts.t: Pets now draw stats from your gear, and every pet family has a unique ability. Foxes are new.
Ranged attacks don't work within 8 yards, and Hunters can't stun or interrupt.
Auto Shot needs half a second standing still before it fires, as in early WoW.

specs.name: Beast Mastery
specs.fantasy: A wild companion at your side, fighting as one with the beasts you trust.

leveling.t: Focused Fire raises all damage you and your pet deal while the pet is out.
The beta's consensus fastest, easiest leveler: your pet tanks while you shoot, so you rarely stop.

group.t: The Wolf's Furious Howl boosts party melee Attack Power (cut by 40% on Sep 24).
Rated a top damage spec at level 30, though some guides note few raid buffs.

pvp.t: Hunters are seen as solid, flexible world-PvP picks; BM itself rates a bit lower.

difficulty.t: The pet does the tanking; the skills are pet control, dead-zone footwork and ammo upkeep.

gear.t: Your pet now scales from your gear, so upgrades help you both.

changes.t: Summon Hawk (16-point) calls up to 2 Hawks to attack your target for 18 seconds.
Pet families learn Bite or Claw and Dive or Dash, on top of their unique ability.
Endurance Training absorbs Thick Hide and now adds pet Health and Armor.

specs.name: Marksmanship
specs.fantasy: A patient sharpshooter: steady breath, distant target, one perfect shot.

leveling.t: Lone Wolf gives 20% more damage with no pet out, so you can play pet-free.
Guides favour BM for solo leveling, but MM has handy tools like Scatter Shot.

group.t: Trueshot Aura now buffs your whole raid.
Lists disagree: top-tier damage on one, mid-pack on another.

pvp.t: Sniper Shot reaches 45 yards and extends your next 3 shots by 10 yards.
Long-range Hunters are seen as favoured in large-scale PvP.

difficulty.t: Weave shots around a stand-still Auto Shot, a 4-second Sniper Shot and dead-zone footwork.

gear.t: Your ranged weapon, Agility, hit and crit drive your damage.

changes.t: Lone Wolf, a new 11-point talent, is built for pet-free Hunters.
Sniper Shot (31-point): a 4-second cast that hits harder than Aimed Shot.
Trueshot Aura moved to the 21-point slot; Careful Aim adds Attack Power from Intellect.

specs.name: Survival
specs.fantasy: A cunning trapper dancing between blade and bow, always one step ahead.

leveling.t: Traps now work mid-fight, and Strider Kick adds a weapon strike plus a 30% speed burst.
Leveling guides still favour BM; few suggest Survival as a first leveling spec.

group.t: Early beta sims sometimes put Survival first, though the author urges caution with early numbers.
In Classic Era, Survival was mostly a utility or PvP tree rather than raid damage.

pvp.t: Entrapment now always roots when your traps trigger, with diminishing returns.
Opinions split: one list rates Survival PvP highly, another calls melee Survival weaker there.

difficulty.t: Weave melee and ranged attacks, time traps and manage positioning around the dead zone.

gear.t: Needs good melee weapons (dual-wield works) as well as a ranged weapon.

changes.t: Strider Kick (21-point) and Lacerating Strikes (31-point) add a bleed to Mongoose Bite.
Expose Prey: attacks on your Hunter's Mark target can enable Mongoose Bite.
Predator's Edge raises melee crit damage and off-hand damage when dual-wielding.

facts.t: Rogues remain the masters of Stealth and the only class with Poisons.
Sap no longer breaks Stealth, and Poisons now stack with sharpening stones.
Guides say Poisons unlock at 20 through a class quest, and in Forever they can crit.

specs.name: Assassination
specs.fantasy: A patient poisoner, letting venom-dipped daggers do the quiet work.

leveling.t: Improved Poisons often saves Poison charges, so you reapply less.
Guides usually steer new Rogues to Combat for leveling rather than Assassination.

group.t: Blizzard: Rogues bring Stealth, control and the highest potential single-target melee damage.
Rated a top melee damage spec, especially on single-target bosses.

pvp.t: Rogues are widely seen as top world-PvP picks: Stealth lets you choose your fights.

difficulty.t: Keep Venom and Slice and Dice up, manage Poisons and pool Energy.

gear.t: Mutilate needs two daggers, and guides call Rogues highly gear-dependent.

changes.t: Mutilate (21-point) strikes with both daggers, hits poisoned targets harder and awards 2 combo points.
Venom (31-point) is a finisher: 30% more Poison damage and more Poison procs.
Cold Blood moved to the 16-point slot.

specs.name: Combat
specs.fantasy: A fearless duelist with blade or axe, trading quick steel for quick victories.

leveling.t: The usual leveling spec: Deflection and Riposte help you chain kills with little downtime.

group.t: Blizzard frames Combat as hard-hitting direct damage with a little cleave from Blade Flurry.
Lists disagree: one rates Combat's damage top tier, another mid-pack.

pvp.t: Opinions split: one list rates Combat PvP top tier, another calls it less effective there.

difficulty.t: A straightforward builder-and-finisher flow, though Energy pooling still matters.

gear.t: Damage follows weapon quality, but Hack and Slash means any weapon type works.

changes.t: Hack and Slash merges weapon specializations: Axes act like Swords, and Maces ignore armor.
Flawless Execution (16-point) lowers Eviscerate's Energy cost by 10.
Combat now supports Backstab builds as well as Sinister Strike builds.

specs.name: Subtlety
specs.fantasy: A shadow among shadows: strike first, slip away, and choose every fight.

leveling.t: Sap never breaks Stealth now, and Dirty Tricks makes Sap and Blind much cheaper.
The Ambush build bursts hard but struggles in dungeons without Cutthroat.

group.t: Tier lists place Subtlety behind the other Rogue specs for group PvE damage.

pvp.t: Improved Distract widens Distract and deepens its stealth-detection penalty.
Rated top tier for PvP: Stealth lets you pick every engagement.

difficulty.t: Openers, positioning, keeping Ambush flowing with Cutthroat, and bleed upkeep.

gear.t: Gear-dependent, and Ghostly Strike and Hemorrhage hit harder with a dagger.

changes.t: Thousand Cuts (31-point): each Rupture tick makes your next Hemorrhage or Backstab cheaper.
Cutthroat: Backstab can let your next Ambush work outside Stealth.
Premeditation is now the 16-point talent; Quietus adds damage to targets below 35% health.

facts.t: Every Priest gets Fear Ward and Devouring Plague at 20, whatever the race.
Blizzard: still the most versatile healer, but in cloth with few escapes.
Prayer of Healing now heals the target's party, and several Priests' Renews can share a target.

specs.name: Discipline
specs.fantasy: A quiet guardian who shields friends before the blow ever lands.

leveling.t: Twin Disciplines boosts instant spells, and Wand Specialization now needs only 2 points.
Method suggests respeccing into Penance at 30 as a sturdy solo bridge until Shadowform.

group.t: Penance was retuned on Oct 8: lower damage and healing, and a reworked mana cost.
Sources disagree: one called Disc the best beta healer, another rates it mid after Penance tuning.

pvp.t: Silent Resolve now also shortens Stun, Fear and Silence effects on you.
PvP lists rate it highly in battlegrounds, a little lower in duels.

difficulty.t: Pre-shielding, Weakened Soul timing and Penance's cooldown reward planning ahead.

gear.t: Holy Precision gives healing Priests spell hit, so you can skip hit gear.

changes.t: Penance (21-point): a 2-second channel that heals allies or damages enemies.
Divine Aegis: critical heals leave an absorb shield on the target.
Soul Warding (16-point) makes Power Word: Shield cheaper, with a shorter cooldown.

specs.name: Holy
specs.fantasy: A steady lantern at the back of the party, mending every wound.

leveling.t: Dual Specialization at 40 lets you quest in one spec and heal in another.
Kills are slow; guides suggest Holy mainly if you level through dungeons.

group.t: Blizzard calls Priests an asset to any party or raid for their buffs and healing.
One list rates Holy top tier for Prayer of Mending; another has it runner-up.

pvp.t: Usually rated below the other Priest specs for PvP, citing few control tools.

difficulty.t: Litany of Light refunds mana when you alternate heals, rewarding variety over one spell.

gear.t: Healing power drives output, hit isn't needed, and downranking heals is now penalised.

changes.t: Prayer of Mending (31-point): a heal that jumps between party or raid members, up to five times.
Binding Heal (16-point) heals you and your target together.
Lightwell is gone, and Twilight Focus gives pushback protection on every cast.

specs.name: Shadow
specs.fantasy: Embrace the whispering dark and wear foes down with patient torment.

leveling.t: Shadowform now halves Shadow spell mana costs and allows all non-healing spells.
Safe thanks to Power Word: Shield, and damage ramps up once Shadowform arrives at 40.

group.t: Shadow Weaving now boosts only your own damage, not your party's.
Lists split: one rates Shadow damage highly, another says it lags; raids untested.

pvp.t: Silence no longer requires Improved Psychic Scream, so it's easier to reach.
PvP lists rate Shadow highly, praising Silence and Shadowform.

difficulty.t: DoT upkeep, plus judging Shadow Word: Death, which hurts you if the target lives.

gear.t: Guides say Shadow doesn't shine until about level 28 without spell power; cap hit first.

changes.t: Shadowform rework: Shadow spells cost 50% less, with a bigger crit bonus.
Shadow Word: Death for every Priest; Early Demise adds crit chance below 20% health.
Devouring Contagion: Devouring Plague jumps to new enemies when its target dies.

facts.t: Call of the Elements drops a saved set of four totems in one cast.
Weapon imbues now last 60 minutes and stack with sharpening stones and wizard oils.
Blizzard: among the sturdiest classes and welcome in any group, but with no real crowd control.

specs.name: Elemental
specs.fantasy: Call the storm down from afar, with molten fury held in reserve.

leveling.t: Key talents moved earlier because Elemental lacked progression moments while leveling.
Viable, but guides flag mana starvation and streaky procs; Enhancement is the easier leveler.

group.t: Buff totems are trained by every Shaman and now reach the whole raid.
Seen as more viable in groups than in Classic; beta lists rate it highly.

pvp.t: Earthbound (16-point): Earthbind Totem instantly roots nearby enemies for 5 seconds.
Rated the strongest Shaman PvP spec on one list, for roots and burst.

difficulty.t: Budget your mana and place totems well, a skill Blizzard says marks experienced Shaman.

gear.t: Guides say Elemental needs steady upgrades, since spell power now comes mainly from gear.

changes.t: Lava Burst (21-point): a Fire nuke that hits harder on Flame Shocked targets.
Lightning Overload: your bolts may fire a free half-damage copy with no threat.
Elemental Mastery returned on Oct 15 as the 31-point talent, with faster casts.

specs.name: Enhancement
specs.fantasy: A spirit-blessed fighter whose weapon crackles with wind and lightning.

leveling.t: Improved Ghost Wolf works indoors, and its second rank makes Ghost Wolf instant.
Broad agreement it's the best Shaman leveler: solid melee, off-heals and Earth Shock.

group.t: Blizzard calls Enhancement damage competitive, and it can tank small groups in a pinch.
Rated strong for dungeon damage at level 30.

pvp.t: No Bloodlust: Rage of the Farseer is a personal attack-speed cooldown instead.
Rated mid for PvP: strong bursts, but no gap-closer or slow of its own.

difficulty.t: Weave Shocks and instant Lightning Bolts between swings; no totem twisting needed.

gear.t: Merged hit and crit, plus Intellect-to-Attack Power talents, make hybrid gear usable.

changes.t: Stormstrike (16-point) empowers your next Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning or Earth Shock.
Maelstrom Weapon: melee hits build charges until Lightning Bolt becomes instant.
Windfury Totem is now a raid-wide buff rather than a weapon enchant.

specs.name: Restoration
specs.fantasy: Guide the tides, letting healing flow gently from friend to friend.

leveling.t: Water Shield returns mana when you're hit or land a spell crit.
Slow solo; guides suggest another spec until Dual Specialization at 40, unless you group.

group.t: Blizzard: Shaman use totems to buff, heal and solve problems for any group.
Widely rated a top-tier healer across beta lists; raids untested.

pvp.t: Rated well in battlegrounds for Nature's Swiftness and Riptide, lower in duels.

difficulty.t: Reactive healing with few instant heals, so positioning matters.

gear.t: Guides list healing power first, then Intellect, MP5 and Spirit.

changes.t: Riptide (31-point): an instant heal plus HoT; your Chain Heal does 25% more on that target.
Water Shield (11-point) is a mana-returning shield.
Mana Tide Totem is now the 16-point talent.

facts.t: Every Mage learns Frostfire Bolt at 40, opening hybrid Fire and Frost builds.
Comprehension, a new Mage-only skill, deciphers scrolls dropped by creatures.
Big-pack AoE farming was deliberately weakened to curb gold farmers.

specs.name: Arcane
specs.fantasy: A scholar of pure magic, each spell setting up a stronger next one.

leveling.t: Sources differ: Method says Arcane may out-damage Frost solo; Warcraft Tavern stresses mana pressure.

group.t: Blizzard: Mages are always useful to a group for buffs, food and water, and control.
Lists disagree: mana holds it back on one, top spec on another; raids untested.

pvp.t: Rated highly for PvP, with Counterspell's silence and Presence of Mind.

difficulty.t: Guides call its new mana-management playstyle quite daunting.

gear.t: Guides say Arcane needs good gear to come online.

changes.t: Arcane Blast (11-point), redesigned Oct 15: each stack grants spell damage, up to 4 stacks.
Arcane Wrath (16-point): a Fireball-sized nuke boosted by 5% of your max mana.
Missile Barrage procs fast, free Arcane Missiles, and is now an early 2-point talent.

specs.name: Fire
specs.fantasy: Build the heat patiently, then let it erupt in one brilliant blast.

leveling.t: Lowest mana use of the three, but low early crit makes it streaky in the open world.

group.t: Ignite is now a separate debuff per Mage, so Fire Mages no longer share one.
Sources disagree: one rates Fire top for burst, another puts every Mage spec mid for dungeons.

pvp.t: Rated strong for PvP: the most burst, but no defensive talent.

difficulty.t: Guides say Fire moves away from one-button play toward reacting to crits.

gear.t: Guides say Fire relies heavily on a high critical strike chance.

changes.t: Heating Up: Fire crits shorten your next Pyroblast; three stacks make it a 1.5-second cast.
Fire Power now adds 1–3% Fire damage per Fire effect of yours on the target, up to 12%.
Ignite no longer loses damage when crits land close together.

specs.name: Frost
specs.fantasy: Calm and controlled, freezing the battlefield so trouble never reaches you.

leveling.t: Frost Blast, a new level-24 slow, replaces the old rank-1 Frostbolt trick.
Most guides name Frost the best Mage leveler: survivability, slows, freezes and kiting.

group.t: Winter's Chill now benefits only you, feeding your own Cone of Cold.
One list rates Frost low for raid damage while praising its control; raids untested.

pvp.t: Cold Snap is now the 21-point talent with a 10-minute cooldown (was 5).
Rated top tier for PvP by one list, thanks to Ice Block and Ice Barrier.

difficulty.t: Method finds Frost easier solo than Arcane; NoobToBoss says it needs more attention than Hunter.

gear.t: Control carries leveling, while Ice Lance burst leans on procs and gear. No guide rates it.

changes.t: Ice Lance (11-point) hits much harder on Frozen targets; its bonus was trimmed to +200% on Oct 15.
Fingers of Frost lets your spells treat targets as Frozen.
Ice Block is now the 16-point talent.

facts.t: Demons now scale from your own stats.
Curses of Agony and Doom are now Banes, so a Bane and a Curse can both run.
Healthstones, Soulstones and Ritual of Summoning remain your gifts to the group.

specs.name: Affliction
specs.fantasy: Plant slow curses, then calmly drain your enemy's strength as it fades.

leveling.t: Improved Drains and Soul Siphon boost drains more for each Affliction effect on the target.
Widely called the best solo caster leveler: instant DoTs on the move, drain-tanking, little drinking.

group.t: Shadow Mastery rose to 10% on Oct 15, a boost to Affliction damage.
Rated top tier for sustained damage on long fights; raids untested.

pvp.t: Curse of Exhaustion is now the 16-point talent, with a 30% slow.
Rated the strongest Warlock PvP spec on one list: slows and drains, little burst.

difficulty.t: Juggle several DoTs, Life Tap and drains; forgiving, because it works on the move.

gear.t: Guides say new talents make critical strike a real Affliction stat.

changes.t: Wrack (31-point): a channel that also raises your other Shadow DoT damage on the target by 10%.
Pandemic: up to +100% crit damage on Corruption, Banes, drains and Siphon Life.
DoTs and drains can now crit.

specs.name: Demonology
specs.fantasy: Bind a demon companion and fight side by side, master and ally.

leveling.t: Improved Health Funnel, Fel Vitality and Demonic Energies help keep your demon alive.
The safest Warlock path once Demonic Brand arrives: your demon holds a few enemies, though it starts slower.

group.t: Demons scaling from your stats keeps them relevant later in the game.
Sources disagree: one calls Demonology the best dungeon Warlock spec, another rates it mid.

pvp.t: Rated mid for PvP; guides favour the Felhunter for Spell Lock and Devour Magic.

difficulty.t: Blizzard says pairing Demonic Sacrifice with Master Demonologist makes a big difference.

gear.t: Your stats now power your demon too, so upgrades count twice.

changes.t: Demonic Pact (31-point): keep your Demonic Sacrifice buff while summoning another demon.
Demonic Sacrifice is now an 11-point talent lasting 2 hours, with new effects per demon.
Demonic Brand and Demonic Knowledge tie your spells to your demon's damage.

specs.name: Destruction
specs.fantasy: Pure fire and shadow, shaped with one intent: end the fight quickly.

leveling.t: Guides call it the hardest Warlock to level solo: hard casts, standing still, more mana trouble.

group.t: Bane of Havoc (21-point): 15% of your damage to other enemies also hits the marked target.
Guides call it the best Warlock spec for dungeons.

pvp.t: Molten Skin, a new talent, cuts damage taken by up to 10%.
Sources disagree: rated high on one list, mid on another, as long casts are easy to interrupt.

difficulty.t: Guides call the rotation demanding and the hardest Warlock spec to level.

gear.t: Hard-cast burst leans on spell power and crit. No guide rates this yet.

changes.t: Incinerate (31-point): a Fire nuke with 25% extra damage on Immolated targets.
Conflagrate is now the 16-point talent; Shadow and Flame links it with Shadowburn.
Hellfire can now crit.

facts.t: Druids can fill any role, but lack snares, silences and interrupts.
In form you can now use potions, racials, and most doors and objects without shifting out.
Tauren, Night Elves and Skyborne on both factions can be Druids; Skyborne get their own forms.

specs.name: Balance
specs.fantasy: A moonlit caster calling starfire and nature's fury down from the sky.

leveling.t: Wrath was redesigned to be cheaper and weaker, then its base damage was raised about 50%.
Guides call Balance viable but slower than Feral solo; some found the early levels hard.

group.t: Moonkin Aura now raises spell crit only, and reaches the whole raid.
Beta lists place Balance lowest among Druid damage options for PvE.

pvp.t: Barkskin and Nature's Grasp now work while shapeshifted.
Rated strong for PvP and called potentially very strong in battlegrounds.

difficulty.t: An Eclipse rhythm of Wrath into faster Starfires, plus DoT upkeep and mana planning.

gear.t: Wants spell power and hit, and caster weapons now carry spell damage too.

changes.t: Insect Swarm (16-point) returns: Nature damage over time that lowers the target's hit chance.
Eclipse: casting Wrath speeds up your next 2 Starfires, stacking up to 4 charges.
Hurricane has no cooldown, and Moonkin Form can cast all non-healing spells.

specs.name: Feral
specs.fantasy: A shapeshifter of fang and claw, prowling as cat or standing firm as bear.

leveling.t: Frenzied Regeneration can now heal up to 100% of your max health, given enough Rage.
Guides call Feral the fastest, smoothest Druid leveling route, though the early levels are slow.

group.t: Leader of the Pack now raises melee and ranged crit only, and reaches the whole raid.
Lists rate Bear tanking and Cat damage mid-tier; Dire Bear and Berserk were out of reach at 30.

pvp.t: Forms are immune to Disarm, and racials like War Stomp and Shadowmeld work in form.
Rated top tier for PvP thanks to mobility and toughness.

difficulty.t: Form switching, Energy and Rage, bleeds, positional Shred, and two roles in one tree.

gear.t: Form damage now follows your weapon's DPS, and weapon enchants work in form.

changes.t: Shifting Power (16-point) turns mana into 40 Energy instantly, a friendlier powershift.
Primal Bite (the renamed Mangle) and baseline Lacerate at 42 give Bears high threat.
Berserk (31-point): Fear immunity, Primal Bite hits 3 targets, and Cat combo moves always crit.

specs.name: Restoration
specs.fantasy: A gentle tender of life, weaving heals that bloom and grow over time.

leveling.t: Bonus healing now also grants a third as much bonus damage, easing questing for healers.
Guides advise against leveling as Restoration, since kills are slow; Feral is the usual pick.

group.t: HoTs can now crit, and Rejuvenation from several Druids stacks on one target.
Called a beta winner: a competitive, scaling HoT healer with Wild Growth.

pvp.t: A mobile healer: Nature's Grasp is baseline and works indoors and in form.
Rated mid for PvP, but expected to gain value in objective battlegrounds.

difficulty.t: HoTs go out ahead of damage, and Swiftmend and Wild Growth reward timing.

gear.t: Wants healing power, Intellect and Spirit; talents help with mana.

changes.t: Wild Growth (31-point): a front-loaded HoT on your whole party, on a 6-second cooldown.
Swiftmend is now the 16-point talent and no longer eats your Rejuvenation or Regrowth.
Revive, an out-of-combat resurrection, arrives at level 12, and Regrowth costs much less mana.

facts.t: Alchemists can set up an Alchemy Lab at your campsite.
Guides say Healing Potions moved to First Aid; Alchemy keeps elixirs and flasks and gains dyes.
Blacksmiths add a Sharpening Wheel to campsites, which Blizzard says boosts Attack Power.
Blacksmithing plans can now drop at random in dungeons.
Weapon enchants like Revelation and Recovery appear in the beta notes.
Enchanter-made wands now sell to vendors for small fixed prices, from 5 copper to 25 silver.
New SAF-T and EZ-Thro explosives arrive; some even work while a Druid is shapeshifted.
Guides say Goblin and Gnomish specializations remain, unlocked at 200 skill by quest.
Herbalists add an Incense Candle to campsites for an Intellect buff.
Rare Scarce herbs like Frilled Lichen go into dyes and some Enchanting recipes.
Leatherworkers place a Tanning Rack at camp, needed for advanced recipes.
Guides say the Tanning Rack also grants rested XP if you have none.
The Oct 1 notes reduced the number of Poor Copper Veins in starter areas.
Guides list a Lodestone camp object for Attack Power, and say ore respawns faster in busy areas.
Each creature can again be skinned only once.
Guides list rare Pristine Leather, Hide and Scale as Scarce skinning finds.
Tailors add a Faction Banner to campsites for a Spirit buff.
Guides say Tailors sew reagent bags for the new reagent-bag slot.

pairs.why: Skin your own hides and turn them into leather or mail you can wear.

facts.t: Guides pair these for Rogues, Druids, Hunters and Shamans: you supply all your own leather.
Leatherworking patterns can now drop at random in dungeons.

pairs.why: Mine your own ore, smelt the bars, and forge plate and weapons.

facts.t: Guides call it the natural pair for Warriors and Paladins: you supply every bar yourself.
Each profession adds its own campsite buff, so your pair helps your whole group.

pairs.why: Turn your own ore into bombs, goggles and gadgets; a PvP favourite.

facts.t: Guides call it a PvP and utility favourite that suits any class.
Gnomes have a racial that makes engineering devices more reliable.

pairs.why: Pick your own herbs and brew elixirs, flasks and dyes.

facts.t: Guides call it a steady gold-maker that suits every class.
Each profession adds its own campsite buff, so your pair helps your whole group.

pairs.why: Sew your own robes, then disenchant spare tailored gear to fuel your enchants.

facts.t: Cloth drops from the humanoids you fight anyway, so this pair needs no gathering skill.
The Oct 15 notes lowered the vendor price of many profession-made items.

pairs.why: Two gatherers: sell leather and ore as you quest, plus rare Scarce finds.

facts.t: Two gathering skills and no crafting, so everything you collect can go to market.
The Bountiful Harvest Legacy perk finds extra Scarce materials when you gather.

pairs.why: Two gatherers: collect leather and herbs on the same route, with no crafting costs.

facts.t: Pure gathering means no recipes or materials to buy; every find can be sold.
The Bountiful Harvest Legacy perk finds extra Scarce materials when you gather.

pairs.why: The classic gold pair: stop for every herb and vein along your route.

facts.t: Guides disagree on whether you can track herbs and ore at the same time.
The Bountiful Harvest Legacy perk finds extra Scarce materials when you gather.

pairs.why: Tailoring uses cloth, not leather, so it's mostly two money-makers, not a supply chain.

facts.t: Tailoring runs on cloth from humanoids, so Skinning simply adds leather to sell.
Guides say Favor vendors sell Tailoring cloth sets for each spell school.

secondary.name: Cooking
secondary.tip: Cooking builds the campfire your group gathers around, and crafted food can now add a small XP bonus.

secondary.name: First Aid
secondary.tip: Level it early: bandages cut downtime, and the Field Medicine Legacy perk shortens Recently Bandaged outside dungeons, raids and battlegrounds.

secondary.name: Fishing
secondary.tip: A calm break between quests, and the Fish Bowl camp object gives your camp an all-stats buff.

safeguards.title: Bring snacks
safeguards.t: Carry food and drink, level First Aid early, and sit by a campfire between fights for its one-hour buffs.

facts.t: Campfires offer rest, vendors, repairs and one-hour buffs; sit by the fire briefly to collect them.
Legacy perks help: Field Medicine shortens Recently Bandaged, and Gourmand makes food buffs last longer.

safeguards.title: Join a guild early
safeguards.t: A guild means steady groups and friendly faces. Forever also has a Group Finder where you can post or browse dungeon groups.

facts.t: The Group Finder lists dungeons and can show every level range (Oct 15 notes).
Group listings carry a playstyle tag, including Learning and Relaxed.

safeguards.title: It's called Forever
safeguards.t: Balance moves both ways over the years. Pick what you love, not this week's numbers; the beta only went to level 30.

facts.t: The beta cap rose from 20 to 30 on Oct 1; nothing above level 30 was tested.
Level-60 raids open Dec 9, so the real endgame picture comes later.

safeguards.title: Take your time
safeguards.t: There's no race to 60. The Well Rested Legacy perk and dungeon runs both help, and every level is part of the story.

facts.t: The Well Rested Legacy perk raises your rested XP cap and fills it faster.
Aggrend: after the fixes, dungeon leveling should be very close to optimal questing speed.

safeguards.title: You're not locked in
safeguards.t: Your class can fill more than one role. Dual Specialization arrives at level 40, so you can quest in one spec and group in another.

facts.t: Dual Specialization unlocks at level 40.

safeguards.title: Try it first
safeguards.t: This spec asks a lot of your hands. Run its rotation in the free Rotation sim before you commit.

safeguards.title: Pair it with gathering
safeguards.t: Two crafts can drain your purse. Level a gathering skill early, maybe on another character, or sell what you gather to fund them.

facts.t: The Oct 15 notes lowered the vendor price of many profession-made items.

safeguards.title: You'll stand out
safeguards.t: {race} made up just {share} of beta characters, so yours will turn heads in town.

facts.t: Beta census: Troll 7.1%, Gnome 7.3%, Tauren 7.7% and Dwarf 7.9% of characters.

safeguards.title: Plenty of company
safeguards.t: {race} made up {share} of beta characters: more groups around, and more people chasing the same gear.

facts.t: Beta census: Undead 17.4% and Human 15.7%, the two most-created races.

safeguards.title: One side on PvP
safeguards.t: On the PvP ruleset your account plays one faction. On Normal and Roleplaying you can play both.

facts.t: On the PvP ruleset, once you create a character of one faction, you can't create the other there.

legacy.title: Just give it a whirl
legacy.t: Play it with immersion and see how it feels. Either way you earn Legacy Points toward your next character: every class earns a point at levels 25, 45 and 60, shared across your account. And you can always come back to this one.

facts.t: Legacy Points are account-wide, shared by all your non-Hardcore characters.
Good to know: each class earns its level points once, so a second Warrior, say, won't earn them again.
Each character can spend up to 16 points at launch, and one character alone can earn 29.

faction: Coin flip: which side are you hoping for?
Which capital do you picture logging out in?
Whose banner would you be proud to carry into a battleground?
Do your friends already have a side? Playing together might settle it.
Which side's story do you want to be part of?
race: Which one do you daydream about at work?
Open the character creator and spin them around. Who made you smile?
Whose walk would you happily watch for hundreds of hours?
Which starting zone do you want to see first?
Which racial sounds the most fun to use, not just the most useful?
class: If it got nerfed tomorrow, would you still want it?
Imagine your hardest fight: holding the line, keeping everyone alive, or burning it down?
Which one do you daydream about at work?
Which ability are you most excited to press for the first time?
Do you picture yourself questing alone, or mostly with friends?
prof: Do you like stopping for every herb and vein, or would you rather keep moving?
Which item would you be proud to make for a friend?
Would you rather use what you make, or sell it and watch the gold roll in?
What would you love to set up first at your campfire?
